newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-WILLIAMS, LARA SPARKLE AGAINST SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WILLIAMS, LARA SPARKLE AGAINST SRI LANKA.

text.p: West Indies, powered by the exciting strokeplay of Stuart Williams and Brian Lara, set Sri Lanka a challenging target of 284 to win their one-off limited overs international on Friday.
West Indies, sent in to bat by the World Cup champions, reached 283 for seven off their 49 overs after the game was reduced from 50 overs an innings because of early morning rain.
The imposing total was built around a scintillating third-wicket partnership of 124 between opener Williams, who made a one-day best knock of 91, and Lara, who stroked 68.
The pair took the score from a shaky 46 for two to a comfortable 170 for three before left-arm spinner Sanath Jayasuriya, who took five for 59 off 10 overs, got the vital breakthrough.
Williams hit 12 elegant fours in his 107-ball innings, just missing his first one-day century, and Lara hit six fours and two sixes in his run-a-ball innings.
After Lara and Williams departed, debutant Floyd Reifer (9) and Carl Hooper (25) tried to sustain the quick scoring against the wily Jayasuriya, who also dismissed both batsmen.
But some vigorous hitting by Roland Holder (41 not out) and all-rounder Laurie Williams (14) provided a useful late flourish.
Earlier, West Indies' decision to sent in pinch hitters Junior Murray (2) and Franklyn Rose (7) at the top of the order back-fired.
